From 19fc99d0c6ba7d9b65456496b5bb2169d5f74cd0 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Nicolas Schichan <nschichan@freebox.fr>
Date: Wed, 6 May 2015 18:31:56 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] ARM: net fix emit_udiv() for BPF_ALU | BPF_DIV | BPF_K
 intruction.

In that case, emit_udiv() will be called with rn == ARM_R0 (r_scratch)
and loading rm first into ARM_R0 will result in jit_udiv() function
being called the same dividend and divisor. Fix that by loading rn
first into ARM_R1 and then rm into ARM_R0.

Signed-off-by: Nicolas Schichan <nschichan@freebox.fr>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org> # v3.13+
Fixes: aee636c4809f (bpf: do not use reciprocal divide)
Acked-by: Mircea Gherzan <mgherzan@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

diff --git a/arch/arm/net/bpf_jit_32.c b/arch/arm/net/bpf_jit_32.c
index e1268f905026..f412b53ed268 100644
--- a/arch/arm/net/bpf_jit_32.c
+++ b/arch/arm/net/bpf_jit_32.c
@@ -449,10 +449,21 @@ static inline void emit_udiv(u8 rd, u8 rm, u8 rn, struct jit_ctx *ctx)
 		return;
 	}
 #endif
-	if (rm != ARM_R0)
-		emit(ARM_MOV_R(ARM_R0, rm), ctx);
+
+	/*
+	 * For BPF_ALU | BPF_DIV | BPF_K instructions, rm is ARM_R4
+	 * (r_A) and rn is ARM_R0 (r_scratch) so load rn first into
+	 * ARM_R1 to avoid accidentally overwriting ARM_R0 with rm
+	 * before using it as a source for ARM_R1.
+	 *
+	 * For BPF_ALU | BPF_DIV | BPF_X rm is ARM_R4 (r_A) and rn is
+	 * ARM_R5 (r_X) so there is no particular register overlap
+	 * issues.
+	 */
 	if (rn != ARM_R1)
 		emit(ARM_MOV_R(ARM_R1, rn), ctx);
+	if (rm != ARM_R0)
+		emit(ARM_MOV_R(ARM_R0, rm), ctx);
 
 	ctx->seen |= SEEN_CALL;
 	emit_mov_i(ARM_R3, (u32)jit_udiv, ctx);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `arch/arm/net/bpf_jit_32.c`**
- The function `emit_udiv()` has been modified to change the order of loading registers for specific BPF instructions.
- A comment block has been added to explain the changes:
  - For `BPF_ALU | BPF_DIV | BPF_K` instructions, the code now loads `rn` into `ARM_R1` before loading `rm` into `ARM_R0`. This prevents overwriting `ARM_R0` with `rm` before it is used as a source for `ARM_R1`.
  - For `BPF_ALU | BPF_DIV | BPF_X`, the original logic remains unchanged as there are no register overlap issues.

### Relationships
- The modification addresses a bug related to the handling of division operations in the BPF JIT compiler for ARM architecture. By changing the order of register loading, the patch ensures that the correct values are used in the division operation, thus preventing incorrect behavior when the same register is used for both the dividend and divisor. This fix is directly related to the previously identified issue in commit `aee636c4809f`, which indicated problems with using reciprocal division in the BPF context.

Here is the commit message:
ARM: net fix emit_udiv() for BPF_ALU | BPF_DIV | BPF_K
 intruction.

In that case, emit_udiv() will be called with rn == ARM_R0 (r_scratch)
and loading rm first into ARM_R0 will result in jit_udiv() function
being called the same dividend and divisor. Fix that by loading rn
first into ARM_R1 and then rm into ARM_R0.

Signed-off-by: Nicolas Schichan <nschichan@freebox.fr>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org> # v3.13+
Fixes: aee636c4809f (bpf: do not use reciprocal divide)
Acked-by: Mircea Gherzan <mgherzan@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

Here is the root cause:
The bug arises from the incorrect loading order of registers in the `emit_udiv()` function when handling specific BPF instructions. When `rn` (the dividend) is loaded into `ARM_R0` (which is also used as a scratch register) before `rm` (the divisor) is loaded, it leads to both registers containing the same value, resulting in incorrect division operations.

Here is the patch:
 
 static inline void emit_udiv(u8 rd, u8 rm, u8 rn, struct jit_ctx *ctx)
 {
 #if __LINUX_ARM_ARCH__ == 7
 	if (elf_hwcap & HWCAP_IDIVA) {
 		emit(ARM_UDIV(rd, rm, rn), ctx);
 		return;
 	}
 #endif
-	if (rm != ARM_R0)
-		emit(ARM_MOV_R(ARM_R0, rm), ctx);
+
+	/*
+	 * For BPF_ALU | BPF_DIV | BPF_K instructions, rm is ARM_R4
+	 * (r_A) and rn is ARM_R0 (r_scratch) so load rn first into
+	 * ARM_R1 to avoid accidentally overwriting ARM_R0 with rm
+	 * before using it as a source for ARM_R1.
+	 *
+	 * For BPF_ALU | BPF_DIV | BPF_X rm is ARM_R4 (r_A) and rn is
+	 * ARM_R5 (r_X) so there is no particular register overlap
+	 * issues.
+	 */
 	if (rn != ARM_R1)
 		emit(ARM_MOV_R(ARM_R1, rn), ctx);
+	if (rm != ARM_R0)
+		emit(ARM_MOV_R(ARM_R0, rm), ctx);
 
 	ctx->seen |= SEEN_CALL;
 	emit_mov_i(ARM_R3, (u32)jit_udiv, ctx);
 	emit_blx_r(ARM_R3, ctx);
 
 	if (rd != ARM_R0)
 		emit(ARM_MOV_R(rd, ARM_R0), ctx);
 }

This results in both `ARM_R0` and `ARM_R1` containing the same value, leading to incorrect division operations when the `jit_udiv()` function is called.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
